# Sabiá-3 Technical Report

Thales Sales Almeida Affiliation: Rodrigo Nogueira and Ramon Pires Thiago Laitz Affiliation: Maritaca AI

###### Abstract

This report presents Sabiá-3, our new flagship language model, and Sabiazinho-3, a more cost-effective sibling. The models were trained on a large brazilian-centric corpus. Evaluations across diverse professional and academic benchmarks show a strong performance on Portuguese and Brazil-related tasks.
Sabiá-3 shows large improvements in comparison to our previous best of model, Sabia-2 Medium, especially in reasoning-intensive tasks.
Notably, Sabiá-3’s average performance matches frontier LLMs, while it is offered at a three to four times lower cost per token, reinforcing the benefits of domain specialization.

## 1 Introduction

This technical report presents the details of the development and evaluation of the Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3 models. We trained them on a large corpus of documents written in Portuguese, with a special focus on Brazil-related resources. Through training, models were exposed to information relevant to Brazilian culture, history, and context. The main objective was to have a specialized model that is aware of the linguistic nuances, societal norms, and regional variations unique to the country. Throughout this report, we show that this specialization allows the models to perform better in knowledge-intensive tasks.

We applied an approach of continual learning by leveraging a “generalist” model that already acquired some level of language understanding and reasoning abilities, and then further trained it on our corpus of high-quality data relevant to the Brazilian context. The development consisted of two main phases: (1) the pre-training phase, in which we further train a pre-trained model on specialized data following a self-supervised learning strategy optimizing for the next token prediction objective, and (2) the post-training phase where the model is tuned to follow instructions and align to human preferences.

Compared to our previous release, Sabiá-2 [[5](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib5 "")], we have collected a significantly larger volume of data for pre-training. In addition to the scale, we also improved the quality of our pre-training data by using a mixture of heuristic and model-based methods to filter out low-quality data.

Considering the challenges of training large scale models, we used TPU v5 accelerators with Jax [[7](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib7 "")] to perform distributed training. We combined both data and model parallelism to achieve high training throughput and to ensure efficient utilization of TPU hardware.

After pre-training, we employed a mix of human-annotated and synthetically generated data to teach our base model to follow instructions [[1](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib1 ""), [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib2 ""), [15](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib15 ""), [16](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib16 ""), [13](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib13 ""), [8](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib8 "")]. The instruction tuning data is composed of both human-annotated prompts and synthetically generated instructions targeting specific capabilities. In addition, we also include synthetic examples to induct self-awareness abilities in the model [[6](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib6 "")].

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3/figs/price_vs_performance_en.png)Figure 1: Price in USD per million tokens, considering an equal proportion of input and output tokens, versus performance on 70 Brazilian exams (in Portuguese). The dashed curve represents a Pareto frontier for general-purpose LLMs such as Llama 3.1 and GPT-4o, which Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3 surpass due to their domain specialization.

## 2 Evaluation

In this section, we compare Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3 with proprietary and open-source LLMs, listed in Table [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report"), on various benchmarks.

### 2.1 Multiple-choice Exams

We have developed a benchmark suite to evaluate the Sabiá-3 performance on 93 academic exams, including entry-level, undergraduate, and professional certification exams. Our focus is on multiple-choice questions from various Brazilian educational assessments, particularly those administered after the middle of 2023 to mitigate the risk of data contamination. However, ENADE is an exception, including spans of 2022 and 2023 to cover a wide range of disciplines.

For more details about the datasets, we recommend the readers to the Sabiá-2 technical report [[5](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib5 "")].
In addition to the 8 benchmarks introduced in [[5](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib5 "")], we now incorporated five new multiple-choice benchmarks:

- •     ENAM: The examination aims to qualify law graduates interested in participating in magistracy selection processes promoted by federal regional courts, labor courts, military courts, and courts of the states and the Federal District and territories. The benchmark covers the first edition of the exam, administered on April 14, 2024, and its subsequent re-application one month later with a different set of questions. There are 160 questions in total.

- •
      CPNU: First edition of the Concurso Público Nacional Unificado (Unified National Public Competition), administered by the Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services on August 18, 2024 for filling permanent public positions. The benchmark includes eight exams with a total of 370 questions, covering the following thematic areas:

  1. 1.         Infrastructure, Exact Sciences, and Engineering;

  2. 2.         Technology, Data, and Information;

  3. 3.         Environmental, Agricultural, and Biological Sciences;

  4. 4.         Work and Public Servant Health;

  5. 5.         Education, Health, Social Development, and Human Rights;

  6. 6.         Economic Sectors and Regulation;

  7. 7.         Government Management and Public Administration; and

  8. 8.         Intermediate Level.

- •     BCB: The BCB benchmark refers to the public examination for the Central Bank of Brazil. This exam features objective questions with two possible answers: true or false. It comprises three distinct exams: basic knowledge, information technology, and economics and finance.

- •     BNDES: The BNDES benchmark is the public examination for the National Bank for Economic and Social Development. Similar to the BCB exam, it consists of objective questions with two alternatives: true or false. The benchmark includes 14 exams covering a range of subjects such as law, systems analysis, administration, architecture, economics, engineering, accounting, and psychology.

- •     CFCEQ: The CFCEQ benchmark is the technical qualification exam conducted by the Federal Accounting Council (CFC). Its purpose is to assess the knowledge and professional competence of accountants who wish to work as independent auditors in organizations regulated by the CVM, BCB, Susep, and Previc. The benchmark comprises 12 exams.

Figure [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 2.1 Multiple-choice Exams ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report") compares the performance of Sabiá-3, Sabiá-2 Medium, and GPT-4o on the ENADE 2022 and 2023 exams. The results reveal that Sabiá-2 has a higher difficulty level in engineering and economics-related areas, as indicated by its lowest 10 accuracies. In contrast, Sabiá-3 shows a significant improvement in these challenging areas, achieving a 70% reduction in errors compared to Sabiá-2, particularly in Economics and Computer Engineering.
Moreover, Sabiá-3 demonstrates a competitive performance compared with GPT-4o, performing equally well or superior in 36 of the 54 Enade exams.
Despite these advancements, the results indicate that Sabiá-3 continues to face difficulties in certain areas, notably Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Accounting, where it reached its lowest scores.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3/figs/Results_for_the_National_Student_Performance_Exam.png)Figure 2: Accuracies of Sabiá-3, Sabiá-2 Medium and GPT-4o on Enade 2022 and 2023 exams, ordered from low to high based on Sabiá-2 Medium performance. Sabiá-3 outperforms Sabiá-2 Medium on 76% of the exams.

Table [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 2.1 Multiple-choice Exams ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report") shows the scores of the models in 13 benchmarks derived from academic and professional exams applied after mid-2023. The results illustrate that Sabiá-3 has a comparable level of accuracy to GPT-4o across all 93 exams assessed. GPT-4o exhibits an advantage particularly in the Medicine benchmarks, while Sabiá-3 demonstrates a notable performance in the CPNU exams. Furthermore, Sabiá-3 surpasses Llama-3.1 405B by 2 percentage points in accuracy, performing equally or better in 62% of the exams. Claude 3.5 Sonnet achieves the highest average accuracy, although it presents a higher risk of data contamination due to its training data cutoff date.

Table 2: Accuracy on academic benchmarks. The average results (last row) cover all the 93 exams applied after the middle of 2023, which is the knowledge cutoff date of Sabiá-3. Claude 3.5’s cutoff date is April of 2024, so exams released before that date might be present in its training data.

In Figure [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S1.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report"), we show the cost per token as of October 2024 in comparison to the average accuracy on the aforementioned exams. We have plotted a Pareto curve based on generalist models, i.e., the ones not specialized in the Brazilian context. Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3 stay above this frontier, underscoring the cost-quality benefits that result from domain specialization.

### 2.2 Conversation Capabilities

This section presents the benchmark we use to evaluate the Sabiá-3 capabilities to engage in dialogues.

In our previous work [[5](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib5 "")], we introduced the Brazilian Chat Evaluation (BRACEval), a benchmark inspired on MT-Bench [[19](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib19 "")] and designed to evaluate AI assistants’ performance in following instructions, engaging in multi-turn dialogues, and demonstrating knowledge specific to Brazil. BRACEval consists of 150 multi-turn questions distributed across 13 categories, including culturally relevant topics such as writing, roleplay, extraction, humanities, entity, and contradiction analysis, as well as universal categories like abstention, harmful content, reasoning, math, and coding.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3/figs/braceval.png)Figure 3: Win, tie and loss rates for Sabiá-3 against other LLMs on the BRACEval conversation benchmark according to GPT-4-turbo as a judge.

Figure [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 2.2 Conversation Capabilities ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report") compares Sabiá-3 with other LLMs on BRACEval. The judge is an LLM that is given the prompt, the answer from Sabiá-3 and another competitor model and decides which one won or a tie. We address position bias by calling the judge twice with the order of two answers swapped.

We use GPT-4-turbo (more specifically, gpt-4-1106-preview) as the judge because, in pairwise evaluations against other models like Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o, all judges — including Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4-turbo, and GPT-4o — consistently preferred the responses from GPT-4-turbo.

Sabiá-3 shows a significant improvement over Sabiá-2 Medium, despite still having a high percentage of losses against more expensive models, such as GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet. A noteworthy result is GPT-4o Mini, which, despite its lower per-token price, achieves a higher win rate compared to the more expensive Llama-3.1 405B in this benchmark.

Figure [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 2.2 Conversation Capabilities ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report") provides a visual representation of the performance of Sabiá-3 relative to other models, across each BRACEval category. We measure the performance using the adjusted win rate, where the winner model receives one point, and in the case of a tie, both models earn 0.5 points each.
Across most categories, Sabiá-3 outperforms Sabiá-2 Medium and performs comparably to the more expensive Llama-3.1 405B model. However, it performs poorly compared to GPT-4o, particularly in coding, math, and writing. This result is consistent regardless of the judge model; using Claude 3.5 Sonnet as a judge yields similar win rates, which indicates that the result is not influenced by the use of GPT-4-turbo as the judge.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3/figs/braceval_category.png)Figure 4: Category-wise adjusted win rates of Sabiá-3 against other models on BRACEval, with 0.5 representing a tie; models that score below it are worse than Sabiá-3; above it, competitor models are superior.

### 2.3 Instruction-Following Capabilities

One relevant benchmark to assess LLM abilities to follow instructions is the IFEval [[20](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib20 "")]. IFEval consists of approximately 500 prompts including instructions that are veriafiable programmatically such as “write in more than 400 words”. It uses two main metrics: strict and loose. In the strict metric, the model’s response is checked against a set of verifiable instructions to determine if it followed all of them. If so, the model receives a point. If any part of the instruction is not followed exactly as specified, the response is deemed incorrect and the model does not receive a point. The loose metric is more lenient as it considers variations and common transformations that might occur in the model’s response. For example, if an instruction requires a specific phrase to be included at the end of an email, but the model includes that phrase with additional text formatting like bold or italics, the loose metric might still consider the instruction to be followed, whereas the strict metric would not.

Since this benchmark’s prompts and target answers are in English, we do not expect our Portuguese-specialized model to yield significant improvements in this scenario. Instead, this benchmark primarily serves to assess how well our model can follow instructions in comparison to state-of-the-art LLMs.

The results presented in Table [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.T3 "Table 3 ‣ 2.3 Instruction-Following Capabilities ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report") show that Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3 outperform Sabiá-2 Medium in terms of instruction-following capabilities. However, it lags behind other models evaluated in this study, including cheaper options such as GPT-4o Mini and Llama-3.1 8B.

Table 3: Results on the IFeval benchmark.

### 2.4 Long Context Capabilities

Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3 can process up to 32,000 tokens in a sequence. Here we evaluate how well the model uses this capacity through the Needle-in-the-Haystack (NIAH) benchmark [[9](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib9 "")], which measures the model’s ability to find answers within a long, unrelated context. The test involves inserting a small piece of text within a larger context ranging from 1,000 to 32,000 tokens, at various depths from 0% to 100%. Since we are focusing on evaluating the performance of an LLM on Portuguese tasks, we adapt this benchmark using the book Dom Casmurro11 1 https://machadodeassis.net/texto/dom-casmurro/11503 as the context. In a random spot within the text, we insert as a needle a sentence that says “O número mágico de Campinas é {random_number}.” (“The magic number of Campinas is {random_number}.”), replacing {random_number} with a 6-digit number. Then, we provide this modified context along with the question “Qual o número mágico de Campinas?” (“What is the magic number of Campinas?”) to the model. Using regular expression, we check whether the model correctly outputs the random number as the answer.

As depicted in Figures [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 2.4 Long Context Capabilities ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report") and [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ 2.4 Long Context Capabilities ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report"), Sabiá-3 exhibited a perfect recall in our Portuguese version of the NIAH benchmark and Sabiazinho-3 reached a recall of 99.48%, consistently locating relevant information within long contexts. We acknowledge, however, that the task, due to its simplicity, may not fully capture the long-context capabilities of language models. Therefore, for a better measure of long-range comprehension skills, we need Portuguese versions of more challenging benchmarks, such as the QuALITY benchmark [[14](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib14 "")], which tests a model’s ability to answer questions about books.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3/figs/needleinhaystack_sabia-3.png)Figure 5: Performance of the Sabiá-3 model in the Portuguese-adapted Needle-in-the-Haystack (NIAH) benchmark.![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3/figs/needleinhaystack_sabiazinho-3.png)Figure 6: Performance of the Sabiazinho-3 model in the Portuguese-adapted Needle-in-the-Haystack (NIAH) benchmark.

### 2.5 Function Calling Capabilities

The Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) [[17](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib17 "")] is a benchmark for evaluating the LLM’s capabilities in executing function calls and using tools effectively. The benchmark is updated periodically, and comprises three distinct subsets:

1. 1.     Non-live: An expert-curated collection of question-function-answer pairs, encompassing multiple languages and complex use cases, designed to challenge the models’ ability to understand and apply functions accurately. The examples are categorized into Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis, measuring whether the function names, arguments, and parameter types match the expected response; and executable verification (Exec), which executes the function and verifies whether the output is correct.

2. 2.     Live: User-contributed examples that reflect real-world applications, ensuring that the models are tested against scenarios that mirror everyday tasks.

3. 3.     Multi turn: Multi-turn and multi-step function calling tasks that simulate agentic behaviors, requiring models to plan execution strategies, request information, and manage a sequence of function invocations to complete a task.

The benchmark also includes two categories to measure hallucinations: irrelevance detection, when none of the provided functions is relevant to the query and should not be invoked; and relevance, when at least one of the functions should be invoked.

To evaluate the models we use the original examples in English. Table [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.T4 "Table 4 ‣ 2.5 Function Calling Capabilities ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report") shows the results of Sabiá-3, Sabiazinho-3, and other proprietary LLMs.
The results indicate that Sabiá-3 ranks competitively alongside top-performing models. It outperforms in the Non-live categories but requires enhancements in multi-turn and multi-step tasks. For instance, increasing the support for more than 32,000 tokens could improve in one of the multi-turn categories. It also needs to improve in the irrelevance category.

Table 4: Results on the BFCL benchmark ordered by overall accuracy.

### 2.6 Agentic Performance

Recent advancements in the ability of LLMs on instruction-following, function calling, and reason in long contexts have enabled the development of LLM-based agents. These agents can automatically execute complex tasks, such as developing code [[18](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib18 ""), [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib4 "")], managing everyday user tasks on operating systems [[11](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib11 ""), [12](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib12 "")], and orchestrating robots [[3](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib3 "")].

To evaluate an LLM in agentic tasks, it is necessary to integrate it with a framework with modules for memory, action, and reasoning. This setup allows the LLM to interact with responsive environments through tools using natural language. To this end, we use AgentBench [[10](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib10 "")], a framework designed to evaluate the agentic capabilities of LLMs across eight distinct environments. It tests the model’s performance in multi-turn open-ended generation scenarios involving coding, gaming, and web.

Here are the eight environments where the agent LLM performs tasks in AgentBench:

- •     Operating System (OS): Interacts with a real Ubuntu terminal, executing bash scripts to retrieve information about the virtual OS.

- •     Database (DB): Runs SQL queries on a database to answer high-level questions about multiple tables.

- •     Knowledge Graph (KG): Navigates a knowledge graph with 45 million entities and 3 billion facts to extract high-level insights about relationships between entities.

- •     Web Shopping (WS): Navigates an online shopping environment to make purchases from a web page.

- •     Web Browsing (WB): Browses web pages across various domains to extract information or perform high-level actions.

- •     Digital Card Game (DCG): Plays a game against a rule-based agent, analyzing cards with different abilities to defeat the opponent.

- •     Lateral Thinking Puzzle (LTP): Solves riddles by asking questions where another agent LLM (GPT-3.5 Turbo) can only respond with “yes”, “no”, or “irrelevant”.

- •     House-Holding (HH): Explores a virtual house, interacting with objects and performing high-level tasks.

Table [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#S2.T5 "Table 5 ‣ 2.6 Agentic Performance ‣ 2 Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-3 Technical Report") presents the results, using the same metrics defined in the AgentBench paper [[10](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12049v3#bib.bib10 "")]. Each environment metric ranges from 0 to 100, with higher scores indicating better performance. We report the Overall Average (OA) across all environments as our primary metric. Due to the variation in mean scores across different environments, OA is the weighted average of tasks scores, normalized to a scale from 0 to 10, where the weights are inversely proportional to the average score obtained by the models evaluated in the AgentBench paper. That is, harder tasks will have a higher weight.

Table 5: Results on AgentBench.

Even though AgentBench is in English, Sabiá-3 shows competitive performance compared to models primarily trained in this language, achieving an OA of 2.9, comparable to GPT-4o Mini. Notably, Sabiá-3 shows an improvement of 2 OA over its predecessor, Sabiá-2 Medium.

Sabiá-3 particularly excels in web-grounded agentic tasks, which involve navigating through web pages to extract relevant information and perform high-level actions. It achieves the top performance in WS, with a score of 62.5, and the second-best performance in WB. However, there’s still improvement to be done in code-grounded environments such as OS and DB.

## 3 Conclusion

We introduced Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3, a family of language models focused on Brazil-related content. They improve upon our earlier Sabiá-2 models, especially in handling long texts, reasoning, and coding. Despite rivaling state-of-the-art proprietary and open-source models on knowledge-intensive tasks while having a lower per token cost, Sabiá-3 and Sabiazinho-3 still have room for improvement in multi-step tasks and following instructions accurately, both of which we plan to address in future work.

# Ministry of Tourism (Brazil)

Federal ministry of Brazil

*Ministry of Tourism*

| [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério do Turismo* | |
| --- | --- |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/MTUAssinatura.png/250px-MTUAssinatura.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MTUAssinatura.png) | |
| Agency overview | |
| Formed | 1 January 2003; 23 years ago (2003-01-01) |
| Type | [Ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_(government_department) "Ministry (government department)") |
| Jurisdiction | [Federal government of Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") |
| Headquarters | [Esplanada dos Ministérios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monumental_Axis "Monumental Axis"), Bloco U   [Brasília](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasília "Brasília"), [Federal District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_District_(Brazil) "Federal District (Brazil)") |
| Annual budget | $826.9 m [BRL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_real "Brazilian real") (2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Tourism_(Brazil)#cite_note-1) |
| Agency executives | [Gustavo Feliciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavo_Feliciano "Gustavo Feliciano"), MinisterAna Machado Lopes, Executive-SecretaryMilton Zuanazzi, Secretary of Planning, Sustainability and Competitiveness in TourismCarlos Henrique Sobral, Secretary of Infrastructure, Credit and Investments in Tourism |
| Website | [www.gov.br/turismo/](https://www.gov.br/turismo/) |

The **Ministry of Tourism** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério do Turismo*) is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") created on 1 January 2003. It is responsible for [Embratur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embratur "Embratur"), the Brazilian Tourist Board.

Developing tourism as a sustainable economic activity with a relevant role for the [generation of jobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment "Unemployment") and [foreign currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency "Currency") and providing [social inclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_exclusion "Social exclusion"). The Ministry of Tourism is innovating in the handling of public policies with a decentralized management model, guided by [strategic thinking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_thinking "Strategic thinking").

Its organizational structure comprises the National Secretariat of Tourism Policies, which assumes the role of carrying out the [national policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Policy "National Policy") for the sector, oriented by the directives from the national Council of Tourism. In addition, it is responsible for the internal promotion and oversees the [quality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quality_assurance "Quality assurance") of the provision of the Brazilian tourism service.

The National Secretariat of Programs for the Development of Tourism is responsible for subsidizing the formulation of plans, programs and actions for the strengthening of national tourism. The duties of the body are the promotion and development of [infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure "Infrastructure") and the improvement in the quality of the services rendered.

[EMBRATUR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embratur "Embratur") – Brazilian Tourism Institute, established on November 18, 1966, as a Brazilian tourism enterprise, had the objective of fostering tourism activity by making feasible conditions for the generation of jobs, income and development throughout the country.

Since January 2003, upon the establishment of the Ministry of Tourism, EMBRATUR's actions were concentrated in the promotion, marketing and support to the trading of products, services and tourism destinations. [[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Tourism_(Brazil)#cite_note-MTUR-2)

- **In office:** January 1, 2023 – Present (Incumbent)

The **Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation** (**MCTI**; [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação*) of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") is the civilian [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil") organization, which coordinates science, technology, and innovation activities in the country. It is headed by the Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation.

## Agencies under the MCTI

- [Brazilian Innovation Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financiadora_de_Estudos_e_Projetos "Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos") (FINEP)

- [National Nuclear Energy Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Nuclear_Energy_Commission "National Nuclear Energy Commission") (CNEN)
- [Brazilian Center for Physics Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centro_Brasileiro_de_Pesquisas_Físicas "Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas") (CBPF)
- [National Institute for Space Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_for_Space_Research "National Institute for Space Research") (INPE)
- [Brazilian Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Space_Agency "Brazilian Space Agency") (AEB)
- [Brazilian National Laboratory of Scientific Computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laboratório_Nacional_de_Computação_Científica?action=edit&redlink=1 "Laboratório Nacional de Computação Científica (page does not exist)") (LNCC)
- [Brazilian National Institute of Pure and Applied Mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instituto_Nacional_de_Matemática_Pura_e_Aplicada "Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada") (IMPA)
- [Brazilian National Laboratory of Synchrotron Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laboratório_Nacional_de_Luz_Síncrotron "Laboratório Nacional de Luz Síncrotron")
- [Renato Archer Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centro_de_Pesquisas_Renato_Archer "Centro de Pesquisas Renato Archer") (CTI)

## 🏆 Vencedores Principais

| Categoria | Vencedor | Desenvolvedora/Publicadora |
|---|---|---|

| **Melhor Direção (Best Game Direction)** | Astro Bot | Team Asobi |

| **Melhor Narrativa (Best Narrative)** | Metaphor: ReFantazio | Studio Zero / Sega |
| **Melhor Arte (Best Art Direction)** | Metaphor: ReFantazio | Studio Zero / Sega |

| **Melhor Atuação (Best Performance)** | Melina Juergens como Senua – Senua's Saga: Hellblade II | Ninja Theory |
| **Jogo Independente (Best Independent Game)** | Balatro | LocalThunk / Playstack |
| **Jogo Indie de Estreia (Best Debut Indie Game)** | Balatro | LocalThunk / Playstack |
| **Jogo Contínuo (Best Ongoing Game)** | Helldivers II | Arrowhead Game Studios / Sony |
| **Melhor Suporte à Comunidade (Best Community Support)** | Baldur's Gate 3 | Larian Studios |
| **Melhor Jogo Multiplayer (Best Multiplayer Game)** | Helldivers II | Arrowhead Game Studios / Sony |
| **Inovação em Acessibilidade (Accessibility Innovation)** | Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown | Ubisoft |
| **Jogo de Simulação/Estratégia (Best Sim/Strategy Game)** | Frostpunk 2 | 11 Bit Studios |

## 🌍 Prêmio Honórico

- **Prêmio Game Changer:** Amir Satvat — por ajudar desenvolvedores a encontrar emprego após demissões em massa na indústria.
- **Cidadã Global do Gaming:** Laura Carter (fundadora da TreesPlease Games) — por seu trabalho em ação climática.

---

## 🎯 Destaques

- **Astro Bot** foi o grande vencedor, levando **4 prêmios** (incluindo o Jogo do Ano), tornando-se o jogo mais premiado da noite.
- **Final Fantasy VII Rebirth** ficou em segundo lugar com **3 prêmios** (Score e Música).
- **Balatro** também faturou **3 prêmios**.
- **Metaphor: ReFantazio** conquistou **3 prêmios**.
- **Senua's Saga: Hellblade II** venceu pela segunda vez consecutiva em Melhor Atuação (Melina Juergens).
- **Neva** venceu o prêmio **Games for Impact**.
- A cerimônia teve audiência recorde de **154 milhões de streams**, superando qualquer evento anterior do programa.

# The Game Awards 2024

Video game awards show

| The Game Awards 2024 | |
| --- | --- |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a9/The_Game_Awards_2024_poster.jpg/250px-The_Game_Awards_2024_poster.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Game_Awards_2024_poster.jpg) | |
| Date | December 12, 2024 (2024-12-12) |
| Venue | [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater"), Los Angeles |
| Country | United States |
| Hosted by | [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley") |

| Most nominations | *Astro Bot**[Final Fantasy VII Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_VII_Rebirth "Final Fantasy VII Rebirth")* (7) |
| [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") | *Astro Bot* |

| Online coverage | |

| ← [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023 "The Game Awards 2023") **·**   [The Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards")   **·** [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2025 "The Game Awards 2025") → | |

**The Game Awards 2024** was an award show to honor the best [video games of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_games_of_2024 "Video games of 2024"). It was the eleventh show hosted by [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"), creator and producer of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), and held with a live audience at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles on December 12, 2024, and [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across online platforms globally. It featured musical performances from [d4vd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D4vd "D4vd"), [Royal & the Serpent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_&_the_Serpent "Royal & the Serpent"), [Snoop Dogg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoop_Dogg "Snoop Dogg"), and [Twenty One Pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty_One_Pilots "Twenty One Pilots"), and presentations from celebrity guests including [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford"), [Hideo Kojima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hideo_Kojima "Hideo Kojima"), and [Aaron Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Paul "Aaron Paul").

*[Astro Bot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot "Astro Bot")* and *[Final Fantasy VII Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_VII_Rebirth "Final Fantasy VII Rebirth")* led the nominees with seven each, and the former led the show with four wins, including [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year"). The inaugural Game Changer award honored [Amir Satvat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amir_Satvat "Amir Satvat") for helping workers in the industry find jobs amid [mass layoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022–2025_video_game_industry_layoffs "2022–2025 video game industry layoffs"). Several new games were announced, including *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*, *[Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergalactic:_The_Heretic_Prophet "Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet")*, and *[The Witcher IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Witcher_IV "The Witcher IV")*. The show was viewed by over 154 million streams, the most in its history to date.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Views-1) Journalists praised the game announcements, developer speeches, and deserving winners, though the eligibility of [downloadable content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downloadable_content "Downloadable content") led to mixed responses.

## Background

As with previous iterations of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), the 2024 show was hosted and produced by Canadian games journalist [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"). He returned as an executive producer alongside Kimmie Kim,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Deadline_Nominees-2) while Richard Preuss returned as director and LeRoy Bennett as creative director and production designer,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Preview-4) and Michael E. Peter joined as co-executive producer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5) The presentation, celebrating the show's tenth anniversary, took place at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles on December 12, 2024,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Date-6) and was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across more than 30 online platforms,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3) including [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), [Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_(service) "Steam (service)"), [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"), [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)"), [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Watch-7) Alternative live streams offering [American Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language") and [audio descriptions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_description "Audio description") were also available on YouTube.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3)

The 2024 stage featured more [LED displays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LED_displays "LED displays") than its predecessors, an intentional choice by Bennett to change the show's look each year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Preview-4) Sydnee Goodman returned as host of the 30-minute preshow, titled Opening Act.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesHub_How-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-FAQ-9) Public tickets became available for purchase on November 1.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Date-6) Future Class organizer Emily Bouchac indicated that the Future Class initiative—an annual list of 50 individuals from the industry who best represent its future, introduced in 2020—would not induct new members in 2024, instead focusing on valuing existing alumni.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-10)

### Announcements

Preceding the Game Awards, several announcements were made during broadcasts by Wholesome Games and the Latin American Games Showcase on December 10,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Wholesome-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Showcases-12) and [Day of the Devs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day_of_the_Devs "Day of the Devs") and the Women-Led Games Showcase on December 11.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Showcases-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_Devs-13) Fewer film and television announcements were made during the Game Awards 2024, instead focusing almost primarily on games; a preview for *[Squid Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_Game "Squid Game")*'s [second season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_Game_season_2 "Squid Game season 2") was aired, but considered secondary to the promotion of the game *Squid Game: Unleashed*.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Hollywood-14) Announcements on released and upcoming games were made for:[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesRadar_Live-15)

The ceremony on December 13 showcased more than 70 games out of 600 submitted, with specific award names like "Most Likely to Make You Quit Your Job and Become an Artist".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesRadar_TGAGWCAGA-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Bleeding_Cool_TGAGWCAGA-17)

## Winners and nominees

Nominees were announced on November 18, 2024.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Nominees-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Nominees-19) Any game released for public consumption on or before November 22 was eligible for consideration,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Eligibility-20) including [downloadable content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downloadable_content "Downloadable content") (DLC), expansions, [remakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_remake "Video game remake"), [remasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_remaster "Video game remaster"), and seasonal content.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_DLC-21) The nominees were compiled by a jury panel composed of members from over 130 media outlets globally;[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Hardcore_Gamer_Nominees-22) ballots were due by November 12.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Eligibility-20) Winners were determined between the jury (90 percent) and public voting (10 percent); the latter was held via the official website and on [Discord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord "Discord")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-24) until December 11.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Deadline_Nominees-2)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Nominees-25) The exception was the publicly-voted Players' Voice, for which voting opened on December 2.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Voice-26) Specialized juries decided nominees for categories like accessibility, adaptation, and [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Epic_Nominees-27) Two awards—Best Esports Coach and Best Esports Event—were discontinued,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Sheep_Esports-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-India_Today-29) while an additional honorary award, Game Changer, was introduced.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_Game_Changer-30) Approximately 112 million public votes were cast overall, a 25% increase from [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023 "The Game Awards 2023").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Viewers-31)

As with the preceding year, the Game Awards partnered with map developer Studio 568 and artists Nighttimes and Spiral House to create an in-game hub world in *[Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite "Fortnite")*, allowing players to vote from November 25 to December 11 for their favorite user-created islands among ten nominees selected by Keighley and his team; the winner was announced during the ceremony.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Fortnite-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Epic_Fortnite-33) The hub world opened with a [photorealistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photorealistic "Photorealistic") "MetaHuman" model of Keighley,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Fortnite-34) for which he was scanned in to [Unreal Editor for Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unreal_Editor_for_Fortnite "Unreal Editor for Fortnite") at [3Lateral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3Lateral "3Lateral") in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Fortnite-35) Several critics found the model strange and [uncanny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncanny "Uncanny").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Fortnite-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_Fortnite-36)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Fortnite-37) Keighley saw the event as "a prototype" for blending the Game Awards and in-game worlds.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GameSpot_Fortnite-38)

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on December 12, 2024.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_Winners-39) *[Astro Bot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot "Astro Bot")* became the third game published by [Sony Interactive Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment") to win [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") (after *[God of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_of_War_(2018_video_game) "God of War (2018 video game)")* in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2018 "The Game Awards 2018") and *[The Last of Us Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_of_Us_Part_II "The Last of Us Part II")* in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2020 "The Game Awards 2020")); its nomination marked Sony's ninth consecutive year in the category and thirteenth nomination overall.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_PlayStation-40) It was the second Best Family Game nominee to win the top prize (after *[It Takes Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It_Takes_Two_(video_game) "It Takes Two (video game)")* in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2021 "The Game Awards 2021")).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_GOTY-41) *[Balatro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balatro "Balatro")* was the first solo-developed Game of the Year nominee (and second card game after *[Hearthstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearthstone "Hearthstone")* in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2014 "The Game Awards 2014")),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Balatro-42)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Balatro-43) while *[Black Myth: Wukong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Myth:_Wukong "Black Myth: Wukong")* was the first Chinese-developed nominee[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Nominees-44) and *[Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elden_Ring_Shadow_of_the_Erdtree "Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree")* was the first DLC to be nominated.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NPR_Nominees-45)

## Reception

### Nominees

Several games saw increased weekly sales following their nominations, including *Final Fantasy VII Rebirth* by 268% and *Metaphor: ReFantazio* by 172%,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Sales-83) and *Balatro* had its second-highest-earning week on mobile and a 100% increase in [concurrent players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrent_players "Concurrent players") on Steam.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PocketGamer_Balatro-84)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PCGamesN_Balatro-85)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Balatro-86) *Balatro*'s nominations pleasantly surprised critics due to its genre,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Snubs-87)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89) though some felt other [indie games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_games "Indie games") remained overlooked outside of their dedicated categories.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Analysis-90) *[TheGamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheGamer "TheGamer")*'s Stacey Henley appreciated that Games for Impact "can finally feel like part of the show" as, unlike previous years, some of its nominees were also named in other categories,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Impact-91) though *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*'s Keza MacDonald found its nominees incongruous and criteria confusing.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Guardian_Nominees-92) Some felt three of the five Players' Voice nominees being [gacha games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gacha_game "Gacha game") justified the lack of more audience-voted categories.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Dot_Esports_Voice-94)

The omission of Future Class was criticized; *TheGamer*'s Tessa Kaur called it "a loss for the industry",[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Future_Class-95) and *[Digital Trends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Trends "Digital Trends")*'s Giovanni Colantonio considered it a troubling indication that Keighley was attempting to avoid controversy and placate the audience in light of an open letter written by Future Class inductees before the 2023 ceremony.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93) Some critics were puzzled by *[Silent Hill 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_Hill_2_(2024_video_game) "Silent Hill 2 (2024 video game)")*'s Best Narrative nomination as it is a remake of [a 2001 game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_Hill_2 "Silent Hill 2").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-AV_Club_DLC-96) *[Dragon Age: The Veilguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon_Age:_The_Veilguard "Dragon Age: The Veilguard")*, *[EA Sports College Football 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EA_Sports_College_Football_25 "EA Sports College Football 25")*, and *[The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Echoes_of_Wisdom "The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom")* were considered among the biggest snubs by some critics and viewers.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Snubs-97)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Shacknews_Snubs-98)

Many journalists and viewers criticized *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree*'s Game of the Year nomination as it overshadowed other games,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Snubs-87)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_GOTY-99)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_DLC-100) though some felt it was justified by its quality and size.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-AV_Club_DLC-96)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Deserves-101) The show's website was updated before nominees were announced to clarify DLC's eligibility, which many predicted was in preparation for *Shadow of the Erdtree*'s divisive nominations;[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_DLC-21)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_DLC-100)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_DLC-102) some viewers erroneously accused Keighley of changing the rules to make it eligible.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Rules-103) Others also felt its eligibility meant DLC was snubbed at previous shows, like *[Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077:_Phantom_Liberty "Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty")* and *[Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Future Redeemed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenoblade_Chronicles_3:_Future_Redeemed "Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Future Redeemed")* in 2023,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Cyberpunk-104)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Destructoid_DLC-105)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Nintendo_Life_DLC-106) and suggested a new category dedicated to DLC would be more appropriate,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_GOTY-107)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesRadar_DLC-108) though *TheGamer*'s Henley argued there are too few annual releases to justify it.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_DLC-109)

Some journalists considered *Black Myth: Wukong* an [outlier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlier "Outlier") in the Game of the Year nominees and were surprised by its success;[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Snubs-97)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_GOTY-99) it is the lowest-scoring Game of the Year nominee in the show's history, with 81 out of 100 on [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Metacritic-110)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Metacritic-111) *TheGamer*'s Tessa Kaur felt the game's biggest accomplishment was its popularity, comparing it to *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")*'s [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") nomination at the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/96th_Academy_Awards "96th Academy Awards").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Wukong-112) Conversely, *[Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_(magazine) "Vice (magazine)")*'s Dwayne Jenkins criticized journalists who questioned its deservedness based solely on its critical reception, despite the positive player response; he argued that such discussions are more appropriate for audiences rather than journalists, who should serve as [neutral intermediaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalistic_objectivity "Journalistic objectivity"), since the awards have no objective criteria.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_Wukong-113)

### Ceremony

*[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")*'s Gene Park called the 2024 ceremony "the best show put on by the Game Awards so far this decade", though he felt the categories required better curation,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-WP_Review-114) and *[Engadget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engadget "Engadget")*'s Mat Smith wrote that "the Game Awards delivered".[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115) *[VentureBeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VentureBeat "VentureBeat")*'s [Dean Takahashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_Takahashi "Dean Takahashi") thought Keighley "redeemed himself" after criticism of the previous ceremony,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Review-49) and *[Push Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push_Square "Push Square")*'s Sammy Barker felt he deserved credit for responding to past criticism, even if some problems remained.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Review-116) *Digital Trends*'s Colantonio called it "the best possible version" of the show, though he criticized the relegation of important awards to the preshow.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*'s Issy van der Velde similarly criticized that the esports winners were announced in quick succession during the preshow without acceptance speeches,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) and *TheGamer*'s Kaur felt the show remained too long and padded with boring advertisements, though found the reveals surprising "for the first time in a long time".[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Surprises-118)

Journalists deemed the winners deserving, including *Astro Bot*'s Game of the Year award considering its polished and joyful gameplay;[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_GOTY-41)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-WP_Review-114)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115) the game's sales saw an increase after its win, according to estimates published by Alinea Analytics.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Alinea-119) Many writers considered the game announcements surprising and among the best to date;[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) *The Guardian*'s MacDonald compared it to "an old-school [E3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3 "E3") conference".[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Guardian_Review-120) Viewers responded negatively to *[Catly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catly "Catly")*'s reveal trailer;[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Catly-121)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Catly-122) the developer denied claims of [generative AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI") and [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain") technology, and shared a draft version of the trailer with journalists.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_Catly-123)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Developer_Catly-124)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Catly_2-125) The musical performances were praised;[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NME_Arcane-126) *[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")*'s Surej Singh called the *Arcane* performance an "emotional and stirring medley".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NME_Arcane-126) Several commentators appreciated the additional time for acceptance speeches, following criticism at the previous ceremony.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) *[Kotaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kotaku "Kotaku")*'s Zack Zwiezen considered Statler and Waldorf the highlight for their humorous interjections and heckles directed at Keighley,[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Muppets-127) though *TheGamer*'s Kaur felt their appearance acknowledged the show's issues without addressing them.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Muppets-128)

Many considered the Game Changer award and Amir Satvat's emotional acceptance speech the show's highlight;[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_Winners-71)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-WP_Review-114) *Rolling Stone*'s Van der Velde thought the award meant Keighley was taking criticism seriously,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) though *TheGamer*'s Kaur and Henley felt its introduction in the same year as Future Class's removal gave the appearance of awarding individuals to reduce the voice of a collective group.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Muppets-128)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Satvat-129) Some Future Class members were concerned the award had replaced the program as "it's easier to control one person's message than the message of multiple years Future Class members".[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Future_Class-130) Some viewers suggested Satvat's role at [Tencent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent "Tencent") made him "part of the problem" with layoffs.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Future_Class-130)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Satvat-131) Four days after the show, Satvat said he had received "countless hateful messages", including [antisemitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitic "Antisemitic") comments directed at his wife.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Satvat-131)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Eurogamer_Satvat-132) Journalists praised [Swen Vincke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swen_Vincke "Swen Vincke")'s speech criticizing publishers who chase "arbitrary sales targets" instead of making games "they want to play".[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_Winners-71)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Muppets-128)

Some viewers interpreted Vincke's comments as criticism of *Black Myth: Wukong*, which was partially attributed to a poor Chinese translation of his speech; some subsequently attempted to [review bomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_bomb "Review bomb") Vincke's game, *[Baldur's Gate 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldur's_Gate_3 "Baldur's Gate 3")*, on Steam,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Vincke-133)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Vincke-134) as well as *Astro Bot* on Metacritic.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NME_Ji-135) [Alanah Pearce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alanah_Pearce "Alanah Pearce") said that a *Black Myth: Wukong* developer cried after failing to win Game of the Year,[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Eurogamer_Ji-136)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Ji-137) though former *[IGN China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN_China "IGN China")* editor-in-chief Charles Young said he was with the developers at the show and none cried.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Gamereactor_Ji-138)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Yahoo_Ji-139)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Ji-140) Following the ceremony, the game's producer Feng Ji expressed disappointment over the loss and confusion about the award's criteria, writing "I feel like I came all the way here for nothing!";[[n]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-142) he said he had written his acceptance speech two years ### Viewership

An estimated 154 million viewers watched the ceremony, the most in the show's history to date[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Views-1) and a 31% increase from the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5) Its figures surpassed the average viewers of the [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII "Super Bowl LVIII") by 30 million, the Academy Awards sevenfold, the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "66th Annual Grammy Awards") ninefold, and the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Series "2024 World Series") tenfold.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Viewers-150) Referencing the viewing figures, [Reggie Fils-Aimé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Fils-Aimé "Reggie Fils-Aimé") called the show "the biggest global entertainment event of our time",[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Viewers-151) though *TheGamer*'s Kaur considered the claim disingenuous, citing the [FIFA World Cup finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_finals "FIFA World Cup finals") and [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), and the fact that shows like the Super Bowl are generally viewed in groups rather than individually.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Viewers-152)

According to *Streams Charts*, the ceremony peaked at over four million concurrent viewers—the most in its history to date and a 10% increase from 2023—across 1,498 channels, including 1.25 million viewers on the official YouTube broadcast and 397,000 on Twitch.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Streams-153) More than 15,900 content creators co-streamed the event, including over 11,000 on Twitch and a record 4,500 on YouTube.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Viewers-150) On YouTube, the ceremony peaked at 2.17 million concurrent viewers (a 28% increase), with over 1.3 million on the official channel (a 35% increase).[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesIndustry_Viewers-154) On Twitter, usage of the [hashtag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashtag "Hashtag") #TheGameAwards increased by 150%, with more than 1.59 million posts receiving 6.79 billion [impressions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impression_(online_media) "Impression (online media)").[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Viewers-155)

# Thiago Laitz

## About

Thiago Laitz developed Exaranker, a neural ranker that uses natural language explanations to rank search results. Laitz is a Research Scientist at Maritaca AI and an Electrical Engineer at Unicamp. They focus on NLP and Information Retrieval, with an emphasis on building Portuguese-language LLMs and efficient ranking systems. Laitz contributed to the Sabiá-3 technical report and created Inranker, a distilled ranking model for zero-shot search. They also developed Bluex, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on Brazilian university entrance exams, and have studied generative models for synthesizing EEG signals in brain-computer interfaces.
